summary: Discovery call to map p95 latency targets, steady-state throughput, and burst token/sec sizing. AmberFall currently on Hosted for dev, evaluating Dedicated for production and Private for regulated workflows. Main risks: cold starts, KV cache warmup, VPC/KMS integration, and unit cost under sustained burst. Agreed next steps: share traces, benchmark harness, run two canonical tests (steady streaming and burst ramp), and reconvene to interpret results.

KV cache warmup and prefix caching
security: KMS, SSO, SOC2, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Alex Hart from Redwood — Sam's with me — how are you all?
[00:06] Javier (AmberFall CTO): Good, thanks. Busy week but good to sync.
[00:10] Sam (Redwood SE): Hey, Samir Rao here. I'll lead the benchmarking and infra bits.
[00:14] Priya (Head of ML): Hi, Priya Kapoor. We're the ML team. Quick context — running a hosted endpoint for our chat assistant, but seeing p95 spikes on longer sessions.
[00:23] Olivia (Infra): Olivia Chen, infra. HIPAA is a concern for some flows, so Private might be needed for that subset.
[00:28] Alex: Cool. Goal today: map your latency SLOs, tokens/sec targets, and traffic patterns so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private and propose a benchmark plan.
[00:36] Javier: For short messages we want p95 around 300–400ms. Longer summarizations we can accept up to 1.5–2s in some cases but prefer sub-second for triage.
[00:45] Sam: When you say short messages — what's the average token counts?
[00:48] Priya: Short inputs ~15–30 tokens, outputs ~40–80. Long ones: context grows to 800–1200 tokens, outputs up to 400 when summarizing.
[00:57] Sam: OK that suggests a lot of streaming bytes. Are you appending context incrementally?
[01:01] Priya: Yes, streaming appends plus a memory retrieval layer that adds extra tokens each call.
[01:06] Alex: That pattern amplifies KV cache importance — warm caches shave p95 considerably for long sessions.
[01:10] Olivia: We saw an overnight cold spike where p95 jumped 2–3s. How do Hosted and Dedicated differ on that?
[01:16] Alex: Hosted uses pooling and fast autoscaling; cold starts can occur if no warm workers. Dedicated keeps reserved capacity so warm workers are persisted — fewer cold starts. Also we can tune min-workers to avoid that.
[01:27] Javier: Cost matters. We have a monthly budget for inference; Hosted looks variable, Dedicated looks cheaper per-token with a commit.
[01:33] Sam: We'll produce unit-cost models. Also note quantization/ batching tradeoffs; 4-bit quant helps cost but may degrade quality on your summarization evals.
[01:41] Priya: We tried 4-bit and saw small regressions on clinical summaries — not acceptable for critical flows.
[01:47] Sam: Understood. You can route critical flows to high-precision instances and less critical flows to quantized variants with Redwood routing policies.
[01:55] Olivia: Security checklist — SSO (SAML), audit logs, KMS. What's supported?
[01:59] Alex: Hosted supports SAML SSO and SOC2; customer-managed KMS is available with Private. Dedicated can be configured with VPC peering and custom KMS in many cases. We'll send the security docs.
[02:12] Priya: For benchmarking, what do you usually ask us to provide?
[02:15] Sam: Two canonical tests: 1) steady-state streaming with your session mix to get p95 and sustained tokens/sec; 2) burst test simulating a rapid fan-in — ramp to peak in ~30s and hold to see autoscale and cold-start behavior. We'll give harness scripts.
[02:28] Javier: Our estimate: peak ~1.2k concurrent websocket sessions, ~350 requests/sec peak, and token throughput up to ~60k tokens/sec for short surges.
[02:37] Sam: Helpful. Is that mostly short-turns?
[02:40] Priya: About 75% short-turns, 25% long-turns. Average tokens/request ~70, bursts higher.
[02:46] Sam: With that mix, Hosted can work but Dedicated gives more predictable p95 and cost. We'll need to simulate the exact mix.
[02:54] Olivia: If we go Private, we need VPC peering and strict egress controls. Any constraints on cross-region failover?
[02:59] Alex: Private supports VPC peering and on-prem. Cross-region failover is supported but requires topology planning. We'll include network notes.
[03:09] Javier: Ballpark — what's streaming p95 for a 70-token response on Hosted?
[03:13] Sam: Ballpark for a 4k-context model: streaming p95 ~350–450ms under normal conditions, heavily dependent on batching and kernel choices. Dedicated can shave 50–150ms typically.
[03:24] Priya: How much does KV cache warmup affect long sessions?
[03:27] Sam: First tokens pay warmup; after that token throughput is much better. The problem is when sessions hop between workers or model versions. Sticky routing or prefix cache helps keep warm state.
[03:36] Alex: We also support prefix caching and sticky routing to reduce KV churn.
[03:40] Javier: For the burst test, what are typical ramp profiles?
[03:43] Sam: Ramp to peak in 30s, hold 1–2 minutes, then decay — that surfaces autoscaling time and cold-start behavior. We'll provide a k6 script and python harness you can run.
[03:53] Priya: We prefer to run the harness from our infra first.
[03:55] Sam: Totally fine — we'll provide guidance and help interpret results. You can also opt for Redwood-run if you want us to operate the test.
[04:02] Olivia: Does telemetry differ between Hosted and Dedicated? We need token-level tracing and per-route dashboards.
[04:06] Sam: Both expose token-level cost and latency histograms; Dedicated can have longer retention and more granular logs depending on plan.
[04:14] Javier: For legal, we need encryption at rest & transit and 12 months log retention. Is that possible?
[04:18] Alex: Yes — Dedicated/Private can support extended retention and encryption controls; Hosted supports SOC2 and default retention, with add-ons for longer retention.
[04:27] Priya: If we target 350ms p95 for short-turns and 1s for long-turns, how big is the delta Hosted vs Dedicated cost?
[04:33] Sam: Approximate: Dedicated can reduce per-token cost by ~30–60% depending on utilization. We'll model it precisely for your traces.
[04:41] Javier: Recommended model family for summarization tasks?
[04:44] Sam: Use higher-capacity open models on fp16 or mixed precision; avoid aggressive 4-bit quant on critical summarization without gating.
[04:51] Priya: How do rollouts and canaries work?
[04:54] Alex: Redwood supports route-based rollouts and canaries with percentage splits and automatic fallback on regressions. We can tie alerts to your eval suite.
[05:03] Sam: For your 60k tokens/sec brief surges, we'll size GPU counts with two reference profiles: "balanced" (cost-effective) and "low-latency" (higher perf). We'll propose counts and expected p95 ranges.
[05:14] Olivia: Hosted BYOK?
[05:16] Alex: BYOK is supported for Private; Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys but we can discuss dedicated encryption options per contract.
[05:23] Javier: Any healthcare customer references?
[05:25] Alex: We can share anonymized notes and architectures.
[05:30] Priya: Timeline — we want bench results in ~2 weeks.
[05:33] Alex: We can hit that. Plan: AmberFall shares traces; Redwood sends harness and cost model; AmberFall runs tests; reconvene.
[05:40] Sam: I'll send the harness and two test templates (steady-state streaming + burst). We'll include recommended thresholds and what to collect.
[05:46] Olivia: Legal will request the security pack.
[05:48] Alex: I'll send the security pack link and cost spreadsheet.
[05:52] Javier: Sounds good. Any potential gotchas you foresee?
[05:55] Sam: Watch out for quantization regressions and KV cold starts during rapid version rollouts. Also network egress from private peering can affect latency if not colocated.
[06:06] Priya: We'll share our eval set for quality checks.
[06:09] Alex: Great. Recap of action items and owners — we'll follow up via the CRM.
[06:12] Javier: Thanks everyone.
[06:14] Alex: Thanks — we'll follow up with the materials by the dates discussed.
[06:18] Call ends.
